name: Brugada Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Brugada Syndrome

criteria.description: Coved-type ST-segment elevation ≥2 mm in ≥1 right precordial lead (V1-V3) either spontaneously or after provocative drug testing
History of ventricular fibrillation, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, or sudden cardiac arrest
Family history of sudden cardiac death at <45 years or confirmed Brugada syndrome
Inducibility of ventricular arrhythmias during electrophysiological study
Unexplained syncope suspected to be arrhythmic

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of type 1 ECG pattern either spontaneously or after sodium channel blocker challenge plus at least one clinical criterion (e.g., documented ventricular fibrillation, family history, or syncope)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Drug challenge with sodium channel blockers (e.g., ajmaline, flecainide) may be used to unmask ECG abnormalities.

imaging: Characteristic type 1 Brugada ECG pattern in right precordial leads (V1-V3)
other: Provocation test with sodium channel blockers (ajmaline, flecainide) to unmask ECG abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Structural abnormalities of right ventricle on imaging
ST elevation predominantly in inferior and lateral leads
Benign clinical course in most cases
Absence of ventricular arrhythmias typical of Brugada syndrome

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
Family history of sudden cardiac death under age 45
references: Antzelevitch C, et al. Brugada syndrome: report of the second consensus conference. Circulation. 2005.
Priori SG, et al. 2013 HRS/EHRA/APHRS expert consensus statement on the diagnosis and management of patients with inherited primary arrhythmia syndromes. Heart Rhythm. 2013.
Brugada P, Brugada J. Right bundle branch block, persistent ST segment elevation and sudden cardiac death: a distinct clinical and electrocardiographic syndrome. J Am Coll Cardiol. 1992.
